newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico says could remove LPG subsidy by mid-year.
newsitem.headline: Mexico says could remove LPG subsidy by mid-year.

text.p: Mexico could eliminate its government subsidies of liquified petroleum gas (LPG) by July, the Energy Ministry's general director of gas said in a statement Thursday.
Mexico has been gradually raising LPG prices by about 2.6 percent per month to ease away from the government's support.
"We believe it will be in July when the programmed increases eliminate the subsidy," the ministry's Francisco Rodriguez Ruiz said.
With the subsidy removed, natural gas will be cheaper than LPG, according to the Mexican Natural Gas Association.

The ministry is aiming to boost the nation's use of cleaner fuels, such as natural gas, and reduce industrial and residential dependence on LPG and fuel oil. LPG is used in most Mexican homes, with domestic sales at an average 265,000 barrels per day in 1996.
Rodriguez said the hikes in LPG will not change the Banco de Mexico's inflation forecast for 1997.
"It should not provoke inflation increases above those already calculated," he said.
Higher fuel prices could affect the tortilla industry, he added.

The nation's subsidy of LPG contributed to a 84 percent drop in profits in 1996 to $27 million for the gas and basic petrochemicals unit of state oil and gas monopoly Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex), according to Pemex chair Adrian Lajous.
